title: Negotiation Guidelines
subtitle: Like any negotiation, it is a process — back and forth, ironing out and amending. Below are a few simple guidelines that can assist you throughout the whole process.
steps: [{"label":"1","name":"Prepare Thoroughly","body":"Research the other party, understand their needs and constraints. Define your objectives, your best alternative to a negotiated agreement, and your walk-away point before entering discussions."},{"label":"2","name":"Build Rapport","body":"Establish a respectful, professional relationship. Listen actively and acknowledge the other party's perspective. Trust and mutual respect create the foundation for productive negotiation."},{"label":"3","name":"Explore Options","body":"Generate multiple possibilities before committing. Use open-ended questions to uncover interests behind positions. The best solutions often emerge from creative problem-solving, not positional bargaining."},{"label":"4","name":"Negotiate Terms","body":"Trade concessions strategically — give on low-priority items to gain on high-priority ones. Keep the discussion focused on objective criteria and mutual benefit rather than personal wins and losses."},{"label":"5","name":"Close & Document","body":"Summarise agreements clearly and confirm mutual understanding. Document all terms in writing promptly. A handshake is good; a signed agreement is better. Follow up to ensure commitments are honoured."}]
